entitlements.notes: Quota verified: "Unlimited complimentary Domestic airport lounge access in India with your HDFC Bank Infinia Credit Card (Primary & Add-on)." Re-read 2026-10-01. The page’s "Click here to know more" links HDFC’s lounge PDF (https://www.hdfc.bank.in/content/dam/hdfcbankpws/in/en/personal-banking/discover-products/cards/credit-cards/infinia-credit-card/airport-lounge-access-program-30sep2025.pdf), which names the programme: "Infinia Primary and Add on Cardholders can avail unlimited complimentary lounge access through Infinia Credit Card Lounge Access Program. Please swipe your Infinia Credit card to avail the complimentary lounge access." with "A transaction fee of Rs. 2 … per visit for Visa cardholders". So the way in is HDFC’s own card swipe, NOT DreamFolks — `programme` above is the old guess, kept only because nothing reads it while the row is partial (see the header). The list HDFC links (lms.hoi.in/lounge-list/hdfc-infinia) is hosted by a third party; its API (loungepass.hoi.in) still returns an empty set, but the page script carries 49 lounges, all in India, Delhi being Encalm Domestic Departure T1, T2 and T3 and Encalm International Departure T3. Where that list puts a desk is now `listedAt`; which lounge in this directory each desk is, is not matched, so the row still opens nothing. Settled 2026-10-02: the PDF heads the benefit "Lounge Access Program within India" and gives it "For Lounge visits within India", and the list includes international-terminal lounges, while the page says "Domestic"; the programme’s terms are taken over the page, so `scope` is both zones within India and `source` is the PDF.

HDFC: "Unlimited complimentary International airport lounge access outside India via Priority Pass for Primary and Add-on cardholders (1,000+ lounges worldwide)." Correctly opens nothing at an Indian airport — the geography is the issuer’s own word.

entitlements.notes: Re-read 2026-09-22. The old note claimed "Axis names DreamFolks for Atlas domestic access in its T&C". It does not: the T&C linked from that very page has zero occurrences of the word. The DreamFolks sentence that does exist sits on an undated marketing page and is an F&B clause about what you receive once inside — "lounge access, food & beverages as applicable under the agreement between dreamfolks and the lounge" — directly beneath the actual mechanism, "You can visit applicable lounges directly & swipe your credit card for access". The page's other DreamFolks mentions are the concierge benefit, a different thing, which is the likely origin of the original error. Practical risk of the old row: telling an Atlas holder to expect a DreamFolks desk flow invites them to skip the swipe, and the swipe is the one step Axis makes entry conditional on. Quotas are 8 / 12 / 18 by annual spend tier (₹3L / ₹7.5L / ₹15L). The ₹50,000 spend gate does NOT apply — Axis names ATLAS on its waiver list. Note Atlas is the one Set B entry whose quota is left blank in the programme PDF; the tiers come from the card T&C. No terms-and-conditions-atlas.pdf exists in the 28-08-2026 revision run that produced one for Magnus and Reserve. Evidence pointing the other way, recorded rather than buried: DreamFolks's OWN site still listed Atlas among the card programmes for BLR 080 Domestic T2 when it was read on 2026-09-15 (see india.ts and docs/research/lounges-dreamfolks.md). That is a DreamFolks-side claim about a desk, not an Axis instruction about a door, and the two can both be true if DreamFolks fulfils behind the counter — which no primary source establishes either way. Axis's own document governs what we tell someone to DO at the desk, so the programme here follows Axis; the BLR row keeps its dreamfolks claim on DreamFolks's own evidence.

entitlements.notes: Re-read 2026-10-01. The Magnus T&C PDF (https://campaign.axis.bank.in/generic/terms-and-conditions-magnus.pdf, cited here until 2026-10-01) still says "please present only your MAGNUS Credit Card along with your boarding pass" and "Effective 28-08-2026, the Priority Pass card will not be valid for accessing domestic airport lounges in India", and now also carries a 15-11-2026 item on renewing memberships. The product page moved to https://www.axis.bank.in/cards/credit-card/axis-bank-magnus-credit-card ("Enjoy unlimited visits to select airport lounges in India."). Axis’s programme PDF (https://www.axis.bank.in/docs/default-source/default-document-library/axis-bank-airport-lounge-access-program.pdf) lists Magnus in Set B as "Unlimited complimentary lounge access" with 20 domestic-departure desks, Delhi being Encalm T1, T2 and T3 — so the eligible-lounge list IS readable now, and 10 of its desks are in this directory accepting issuer-direct (the "0 of 40" below is out of date). What still keeps the row partial: the ₹50,000-in-the-previous-3-months gate (Magnus is not on the waiver list) has no milestone rule to point at, and each quarter carries a limit "determined by Axis Bank". Earlier: re-read 2026-09-22 against Axis's own documents, correcting three errors. (1) The programme is Axis's own card-swipe scheme, not DreamFolks — you present the Magnus card, not a pass. (2) The 28-08-2026 revision was a CREDENTIAL change, not a withdrawal: "Effective 28-08-2026, the Priority Pass card will not be valid for accessing domestic airport lounges in India" / "please present only your MAGNUS Credit Card". Domestic access is alive. (3) Guests are 4 a calendar year, not none — superseded 2026-10-01: those 4 are Priority Pass guests, and the domestic programme is cardholder-only. The gate binds Magnus specifically: Axis waives it for Burgundy Private, RESERVE, Olympus, Primus, Horizon and ATLAS, and Magnus is absent from that list. "Unlimited" is Axis's marketing word and its own terms contradict it — access is "subject to access limits/quota every quarter … determined by Axis Bank in its absolute discretion", undisclosed. Axis also contradicts itself in public: the travel-stay page still tells you to use Priority Pass domestically, undated, against a dated card-specific revision saying the opposite. STILL HIDDEN, for two reasons that are not about the card: no lounge in this directory records accepting issuer-direct (0 of 40), so a corrected row would match no desk until Axis's eligible-lounge list is read into the directory; and the ₹50,000 gate has no rule in the milestones dataset to reference, which is where a gate must live. The quota is carried as "unlimited" because that is the word Axis prints in its eligible-card list, while its own rules reserve an undisclosed quarterly cap — neither figure can be shown as fact.

Hidden for the same reason as ELITE’s domestic row — the programme depends on the holder’s network. Re-read 2026-10-01, and that reason is now out of date: the card page still says "8 complimentary domestic airport lounge visits (max. 2 visits per quarter)" and still links the network lists, but SBI’s lounge page (https://www.sbicard.com/en/personal/benefits/airport-lounge-access.page) puts "SBI Card PRIME" in Set B, with SBI’s own list of 30 domestic lounges "w.e.f. 10 Jan’26" (Delhi: Encalm Domestic T1 and T3, International T3), entered by presenting the card, which must authorise on the lounge’s POS terminal. SBI contradicts itself between the two pages; the dated Set B list is the more specific. Where that list puts a desk is now `listedAt`; no desk is matched to a lounge here, so `programme` stays the old placeholder (never read while partial) and the row opens nothing. The quarterly ceiling still stands: the card page’s expanded lounge benefit, rendered 2026-10-01, reads "8 complimentary domestic airport lounge visits (max. 2 visits per quarter)".

Unlimited Priority Pass access outside India; inside India the same pass is chargeable at US$35 a visit, which is not complimentary access and is therefore not modelled as opening anything. Amex also grants its own Centurion, Delta Sky Club, Plaza Premium and Lufthansa lounges — none of those programmes is yet provable against a lounge in this directory. The bank's two ceilings disagree with each other - two a quarter would be eight a year - and both are recorded as written, so the annual four is what binds and the quarterly two caps any single quarter.
